routes.description: Establish that naturalism combined with evolution makes the reliability of human cognitive faculties low or inscrutable, that recognizing this condition defeats trust in those faculties, and that the defeater extends to the beliefs supporting naturalism and evolution themselves.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the reliability premise is supported through the separation of adaptive behavior from true content, awareness of low or inscrutable reliability is shown to generate a faculty-wide defeater, and that defeater is shown to include belief in naturalism and evolution.

motionBridge.description: Connect the reliability concern to a defeater for trusting the cognitive faculties of a believer who accepts naturalism and evolution.

centralBridges.description: Show that selection for adaptive neurology and behavior does not by itself select for true belief content.
Derive low or inscrutable overall cognitive reliability from the alleged independence of adaptive success and belief truth.
Explain why recognizing low or inscrutable reliability defeats confidence in faculty-produced beliefs, including the naturalistic evolutionary outlook.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish the determination or supervenience of content from correspondence between that content and adaptive action.
Explain why the proposed reliability defeater is specific to naturalism rather than evolution alone, including the claimed theistic basis for expecting reliable faculties.

routes.description: Resist the alleged defeater by explaining how conceptual and causal relations among belief, neurology, behavior, and environment permit unguided evolution to favor truth-conducive cognition, while challenging the claimed special skeptical disadvantage of naturalism.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if adaptive selection is shown capable of favoring generally true beliefs, the inference to low or inscrutable reliability is thereby blocked, or the resulting skeptical problem is shown not to establish a distinctive defeater for naturalistic believers.

motionBridge.description: Show that naturalism and evolution do not require their believers to acquire the alleged defeater for trusting their cognitive faculties.

centralBridges.description: Explain how accurate beliefs about relevant environmental conditions can systematically support fitness-enhancing behavior.
Show that causal, conceptual, and behavioral constraints prevent belief content from being freely detached from adaptive action.
Test whether the proposed skeptical structure uniquely burdens naturalism by considering an analogous undercutting problem for theism.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Clarify that atheism does not entail naturalism and therefore does not define the full population reached by the argument.
Distinguish generally truth-conducive evolved cognition from any requirement that every evolved belief be true.

sections.title: Adaptive Selection and Truth-Conducive Cognition
sections.rationale: The principal clash concerns whether fitness-enhancing behavior supplies an evolutionary route to generally accurate representation or remains indifferent to belief truth.

sections.title: Mental Content, Neurology, and Behavioral Constraints
sections.rationale: The reliability premise depends on whether content can vary independently of adaptive neural output or is constrained by its causal and conceptual role in behavior.

sections.title: Probability of Reliable Cognitive Faculties
sections.rationale: The debate requires an account of how claims about individual belief truth aggregate into a judgment that evolved cognitive faculties are reliable, unreliable, or inscrutable.

sections.title: Defeater Generation and Epistemic Self-Reference
sections.rationale: Even if reliability is doubtful, the motion turns on whether awareness of that doubt defeats faculty trust and extends to the naturalistic evolutionary beliefs that produced it.

sections.title: Worldview Scope and Theistic Symmetry
sections.rationale: The scope and distinctiveness of the argument depend on how naturalism differs from atheism and whether a parallel faculty-undermining problem arises for the proposed theistic alternative.

precisionFindings.rationale: The limited total-evidence claim is clear, stable, and carefully distinguished from denying any evidential force to suffering.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Plantinga concedes that suffering may count against Christian theism while denying that it settles the total evidential picture.

charity.alternative: Law needs strong undercutting grounds against the reliability-guaranteeing God, not a deductive revelation that no God exists.
charity.decisiveQualification: Plantinga still correctly notes that the strength of those grounds must be assessed against total evidence.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The adjudicated raw ledger applies the preregistered rounded mean to the two nondisputed logicalCoherence values (90 and 94); their difference did not meet a semantic or magnitude dispute trigger.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The evidential principle is well supported conceptually, though the favorable considerations composing the larger picture are not developed here.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly attacks the central skeptical-parity bridge by contesting the premise needed for the alleged theistic undercutting loop.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move grants the strongest limited evidential point and identifies precisely the missing total-evidence qualification.

responsiveness.rationale: The response directly contacts the decisive premise, grants its strongest limited form, and explains why the stronger skeptical conclusion does not follow.

moves.evidenceBasis: Plantinga concedes suffering may count against Christian theism but insists it is only one strand within a larger evidential picture.

moves.speaker: Stephen Law
moves.proposition: The EAAN's reliability challenge is not insurmountable because a naturalist can explain why unguided evolution would tend to favor true beliefs, thereby resisting the inference that evolved cognitive faculties are probably unreliable or inscrutable.

sourceSpan.excerpt: evolved um and uh i i think the the fight the diversion that we've seen today is certainly a challenge but i can't see that it's an insurmountable challenge and and i sketched out some reasons for thinking that it's it's really not an insurmountable challenge that we can as as if i you know if i were a naturalist um a naturalist probably can show why unguided evolution will tend to favor true beliefs

moves.attributionBasis: The moderator explicitly turns to Stephen, who then restates the EAAN’s intended defeater structure before giving his naturalistic response.

components.text: Defeat the inference that naturalism and evolution make reliable cognition low or inscrutable in probability.
Explain why unguided evolution tends to favor true beliefs despite selection for adaptive behavior.
Answer the claim that chance-level individual truth odds compound into unreliable faculties.

response.rationale: Law directly denies that the challenge is insurmountable and invokes his earlier truth-fitness mechanism, contacting the main low-reliability premise but not separately answering the aggregate even-odds model.

precisionFindings.rationale: The conclusion is recoverable and cautiously scoped as a tendency and a surmountable challenge rather than a proof of infallibility.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Law expressly frames the case as reasons for thinking the challenge is not insurmountable, matching the limited support recalled.

charity.alternative: The pro argument permits adaptive neural output accompanied by false content and therefore denies a necessary truth-fitness link.
charity.decisiveQualification: Law needs only a systematic evolutionary tendency toward truth, not a necessary link or universal accuracy.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The adjudicated raw ledger applies the preregistered rounded mean to the two nondisputed logicalCoherence values (84 and 79); their difference did not meet a semantic or magnitude dispute trigger.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The adjudicated raw ledger applies the preregistered rounded mean to the two nondisputed evidenceWarrant values (72 and 69); their difference did not meet a semantic or magnitude dispute trigger.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly attacks the central low-reliability bridge and connects that attack to the evolutionary truth-fitness mechanism.

representationalCharity.rationale: The summary retains the central rival concern but understandably compresses the detailed content-detachment dispute.

responsiveness.rationale: This partial answer contacts the decisive low-reliability and selection components, but leaves the later compound-probability component unaddressed.

moves.evidenceBasis: Law summarizes that a naturalist can explain why unguided evolution tends to favor true beliefs, making the EAAN challenge surmountable.

moves.speaker: Stephen Law
moves.proposition: Even if naturalism results in global skepticism, theism gains no comparative epistemic advantage when faculties supposedly supplied by God yield strong grounds against that God and thereby undercut trust in the faculties themselves.

sourceSpan.excerpt: even if it turns out that um we're gonna have you know we're admired in skepticism as naturalists um we we can't know anything it doesn't follow that theism is in any better position because it may be that as i pointed out theism is in much the same uh skeptical soup uh it's if we have uh if there is a god and he's given us we suppose has given us reliable cognitive faculties when we apply them they appear to reveal very good grounds

moves.attributionBasis: Law explicitly introduces this as his other point and develops the first-person naturalist comparison through the end of his summary.

components.text: Whether theism has a comparative epistemic advantage because God supplies reliable cognitive faculties.
Whether the global skeptical consequence uniquely disadvantages naturalism.
Whether total-evidence qualification defeats the claimed theistic undercutting problem.

response.rationale: Law directly reasserts comparative skeptical parity, but does not answer Plantinga's immediately preceding total-evidence objection to the crucial anti-theistic premise.

precisionFindings.rationale: The comparative claim is clear, but 'very good grounds' is unspecific and its relationship to total evidence remains unstable.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The possibility framing is cautious, but the move presumes strong anti-theistic grounds without responding to their disputed evidential sufficiency.

charity.alternative: Suffering may be counterevidence within a broader theistic case without defeating belief in the God grounding general reliability.
charity.decisiveQualification: The skeptical loop requires net defeating evidence against God, not merely some apparently strong adverse evidence.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The adjudicated raw ledger applies the preregistered rounded mean to the two nondisputed logicalCoherence values (69 and 72); their difference did not meet a semantic or magnitude dispute trigger.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The adjudicated raw ledger applies the preregistered rounded mean to the two nondisputed evidenceWarrant values (58 and 60); their difference did not meet a semantic or magnitude dispute trigger.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the central skeptical-parity bridge, notwithstanding its incomplete response to the latest objection.

representationalCharity.rationale: The adjudicated raw ledger applies the preregistered rounded mean to the two nondisputed representationalCharity values (62 and 63); their difference did not meet a semantic or magnitude dispute trigger.

responsiveness.rationale: Within partial answers, it contacts the comparative and defeater components but leaves the decisive total-evidence reply unanswered.

moves.evidenceBasis: Law argues that even global naturalistic skepticism gives theism no advantage if supposedly reliable faculties produce strong grounds against God.

moves.speaker: Alvin Plantinga
moves.proposition: No adequate grounds have been supplied for assuming that neurology selected for adaptive behavior would also determine true belief content under materialism, naturalism, and evolution.

sourceSpan.excerpt: adaptive behavior will also produce if it produces belief content at all true belief content i don't see the grounds for that judgment i mean i'm inclined to think one would would think that just because that's how we think about ourselves but uh we can't really import how we think about ourselves as things actually stand into the argument in that way because what it's really about is what things would be like if uh materialism and naturalism

components.text: Whether Law supplied adequate grounds that selected adaptive neurology would tend to determine true content.
Whether conceptual constraints justify a truth link rather than merely restricting content attribution.
Whether causal and behavioral association adequately grounds true content.

response.rationale: Plantinga directly challenges the missing warrant behind Law's truth tendency and warns against importing actual-world self-conceptions into the counterfactual antecedent.

precisionFindings.rationale: The negative burden claim is fully recoverable and explicitly limited to the materialist-naturalist-evolutionary supposition.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Plantinga says he does not see sufficient grounds, a cautious force appropriate to the identified explanatory gap.

charity.alternative: Law's truth link rests on environmental success and behavioral-role constraints, not merely ordinary self-understanding.
charity.decisiveQualification: Those considerations provide some grounds even if they do not conclusively establish broad reliability.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The adjudicated raw ledger applies the preregistered rounded mean to the two nondisputed logicalCoherence values (84 and 88); their difference did not meet a semantic or magnitude dispute trigger.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The identified gap is real, but the move does not fully engage Law's strongest environmental and content-constraint mechanisms.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly attacks the central content-constraints bridge and the concluding evolutionary truth-fitness claim.

representationalCharity.rationale: Plantinga accurately presses the missing bridge but somewhat understates the concrete resource-seeking and constraint-based grounds Law supplied.

responsiveness.rationale: Within full answers, it explicitly contacts the decisive warrant question, though it mainly demands support rather than supplying a rival model.

moves.evidenceBasis: Plantinga says no adequate grounds were given for assuming adaptive neurology produces true content and rejects importing ordinary self-conceptions.
